sections.heading: A CRM shaped around customer journeys
sections.body:
When sales and service teams cannot see the same customer history, CRM change needs more than configuration. Linkfields brings consulting, implementation, integration, migration and support together around agreed Salesforce journeys.

Establish the process baseline, user and data readiness, then a prioritised roadmap with acceptance criteria.
sections.secondaryBody: Plan lead-to-opportunity visibility, service case routing and knowledge, and customer or partner self-service connected to ERP. Confirm the required Salesforce clouds, data ownership, user roles and acceptance measures during discovery, then agree implementation and integration responsibilities. [Explore Intelligent Enterprise Platforms](/services/intelligent-enterprise-platforms).

sections.heading: Customer data and access governed from design
sections.body:
Assign ownership of customer identifiers, record quality and data retention. Review identity, permissions and consent where relevant, then test the full journey and its exception paths before release.

[Cyber Security](/services/cyber-security), [Quality engineering](/services/digital-transformation/quality-engineering) and [delivery accelerators](/products-and-accelerators/delivery-accelerators) support agreed assurance workstreams. Adoption, training and hypercare gates make readiness a business decision, not just a technical one.

sections.heading: Questions before you begin
sections.description: Bring your current CRM, customer journey priorities and ERP interfaces to define a practical starting point.

items.title: Which Salesforce clouds and journeys are included?
items.description: Agree the customer process and exact application scope during discovery. Sales, service and self-service journeys are starting points; industry clouds and additional data applications require separately confirmed capability, licences, interfaces and responsibilities.

items.title: Is Salesforce replacing our ERP?
items.description: This is a CRM and customer-engagement offer. Decide which application owns orders, invoices, customers and service records. An integration plan connects customer work to the ERP without blurring those responsibilities.

items.title: How do migration routes differ?
items.description: A third-party CRM migration requires data mapping, cleansing, test loads and reconciliation. Classic-to-Lightning change requires its own workflow, interface and adoption assessment. The route and acceptance evidence depend on the current estate.

items.title: What engagement and support options are available?
items.description: Use Time & Materials for discovery or changing scope; Fixed Price for agreed milestones and acceptance. Managed Service or a Dedicated Team supports continuing operations under agreed boundaries. Outcome-Based terms require measurable evidence. [Explore engagement models](/company/our-approach#engagement-models); Linkfields software is available separately.
